news.title: Putin's Crimea bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
news.summary: Ukraine says the attack took weeks to plan, while the Kremlin vows to rebuild the strategic bridge.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Putin's Crimea bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
news.summaryTr: Ukraine says the attack took weeks to plan, while the Kremlin vows to rebuild the strategic bridge.
news.articleText: Putin's Crimea bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine - Published Ukraine has severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, in what Volodymyr Zelensky says was an "unprecedented operation" weeks in the making. Images shared by Ukrainian officials show a section of the Crimean Bridge - also known as the Kerch Bridge - has collapsed into the water, dealing a logistical and symbolic blow to Russia's war effort. The Kremlin said it would rebuild the bridge "better than before" and that Russian President Vladimir Putin had been briefed on the attack, though he is yet to comment. Elsewhere, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the Northern and Southern bridges, both important crossings over the Dnipro River, were closed after Russia targeted the Ukrainian capital overnight. Ukraine has long targeted the Crimean Bridge, which provides a road and rail route for Russian soldiers heading towards the front line, but has struggled to close it for good. The damage reported on Tuesday appeared to be far more severe than previously, with a large arched section of the bridge apparently destroyed. Video footage appeared to show critical damage to the road section, with remnants of the support arch and road deck seen protruding from the water below. Zelensky said the overnight strike was the result of a seven-stage operation by the military and security services, which saw Ukrainian forces "gradually destroy air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment, and other designated targets on the way to the final objective". He said the rail section parallel to the bridge's road had also been hit by a wave of drones, though images showed its supporting arch was still standing and a Russian-backed official said some rail services were operating. The Security Service of Ukraine said operations had "systematically suppressed enemy air defence systems" over a month, and said it showed "no Russian defence systems can guarantee the safety of illegal objects occupied by the invaders". The bridge was built by Russia after it invaded and annexed the peninsula in 2014, and was personally opened by Putin in 2018. While Ukraine has been trying to increase the cost to Russia of waging war economically, by hitting oil refineries and depots, striking the bridge is an attempt to increase the political cost on Putin. The timing of the strike comes at a significant moment, ahead of Putin meeting the leaders of China and the US. This could cloud his moment back in the spotlight. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge would "be restored following Ukrainian strikes, and it will be even better than before", and did not rule out the possibility the strikes were linked to Putin's visit to China. Russia's Investigative Committee confirmed structural damage and said it had opened a "criminal case... on terrorism charges" after attacks by "Ukraine's armed formations". For the second day in a row, Russia recorded the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, with 2,256 drones downed, according to the defence ministry. Zelensky had warned of major attacks in the days leading up to a meeting between Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in China's Shenzhen on Thursday. Loud explosions were heard in Kyiv just before midnight on Tuesday, with Klitschko saying shortly after that the city had suffered "damage to critical infrastructure systems" and disruption to heating and water. Some of Kyiv's above-ground subway services were damaged in the overnight attacks, officials said, after civilians were told to go to civil defence shelters. Eight major bridges span the Dnipro River connecting the western and eastern parts of Kyiv, and an estimated three million residents rely on the bridges to travel across the city. Strikes on the busy Northern and Southern Bridges will cause major disruption to people's daily lives. Elsewhere, three people have been injured in a Russian missile attack in the Cherkasy region, according to local officials. The long-term impact of the Crimean Bridge strike is still not fully clear though the risk of a serious transport and logistics crisis for the Russian military has increased significantly. The collapse of the arched section of the Crimean Bridge has cut off the peninsula's direct road and rail links with Russia – at least until the crossing can be repaired. However, there is still a land corridor running through the occupied parts of the Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions - though Ukraine has been systematically striking transport routes across northern Crimea, as well as bridges and other crossings in the area around Chongar. This has already caused problems with the delivery of fuel and other supplies, including military cargo. There is a ferry crossing across the Kerch Strait. It could partly compensate for the loss of the bridge, but its capacity is very limited and it is also vulnerable to attack. Russia could also supply Crimea by sea, but this route is also risky, as Ukrainian naval and aerial drones operate extensively in the area. In addition, debris from the Crimean Bridge – particularly its enormous arch – may have blocked the shipping channel. This would make it harder for larger vessels to pass through and create further problems for ports in the Sea of Azov, including Mariupol and Berdiansk. Russia's launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine is now under Russian occupation and Kyiv has refused Putin's demand to give up areas of Ukraine's eastern Donbas that remain under its control. Elsewhere, three people have been injured in a Russian missile attack in the Cherkasy region, according to local officials. The long-term impact of the Crimean Bridge strike is still not fully clear though the risk of a serious transport and logistics crisis for the Russian military has increased significantly. The collapse of the arched section of the Crimean Bridge has cut off the peninsula's direct road and rail links with Russia – at least until the crossing can be repaired. However, there is still a land corridor running through the occupied parts of the Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions - though Ukraine has been systematically striking transport routes across northern Crimea, as well as bridges and other crossings in the area around Chongar. This has already caused problems with the delivery of fuel and other supplies, including military cargo. There is a ferry crossing across the Kerch Strait. It could partly compensate for the loss of the bridge, but its capacity is very limited and it is also vulnerable to attack. Russia could also supply Crimea by sea, but this route is also risky, as Ukrainian naval and aerial drones operate extensively in the area. In addition, debris from the Crimean Bridge – particularly its enormous arch – may have blocked the shipping channel. This would make it harder for larger vessels to pass through and create further problems for ports in the Sea of Azov, including Mariupol and Berdiansk. Russia's launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine is now under Russian occupation and Kyiv has refused Putin's demand to give up areas of Ukraine's eastern Donbas that remain under its control. news.titleTr: Otomotivciler Almanya yolunda: Bakan Bolat'tan 'Made in EU' hamlesi
news.summaryTr: Avrupa Birliği'nin 'Made in EU' düzenlemesinde Türkiye'nin kapsam dışında kalma ihtimali otomotiv sektörünü harekete geçirdi. Ticaret Bakanı Ömer Bolat, sektör temsilcileriyle birlikte kritik görüşmeler için Almanya'ya gidiyor.
news.articleText: Otomotivciler Almanya yolunda: Bakan Bolat'tan 'Made in EU' hamlesi - Avrupa Birliği'nin 'Made in EU' düzenlemesinde Türkiye'nin kapsam dışında kalma ihtimali otomotiv sektörünü harekete geçirdi. Ticaret Bakanı Ömer Bolat, sektör temsilcileriyle birlikte kritik görüşmeler için Almanya'ya gidiyor. Avrupa Birliği'nin (AB) sanayisini korumaya yönelik yeni düzenleme hazırlıkları, Türkiye'nin en önemli ihracat sektörlerinden otomotivde endişe yarattı. Bazı Avrupa ülkelerinin Türkiye'de üretilen ürünleri "Made in EU" kapsamı dışında tutmaya yönelik girişimleri üzerine Ankara ve otomotiv sektörü diplomasi trafiğini hızlandırdı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Ticaret Bakanı Ömer Bolat'ın öncülüğünde, Uludağ Otomotiv Endüstrisi İhracatçıları Birliği (OİB) ve önde gelen otomotiv üreticilerinin temsilcilerinden oluşan heyet, perşembe günü Almanya'ya gidecek. Heyetin, Almanya Ekonomi ve Enerji Bakanı Katherina Reiche ile Türkiye'de yatırımları bulunan büyük otomotiv şirketlerinin yöneticileriyle bir araya gelmesi planlanıyor. Türkiye'nin kapsam dışında kalma riski Avrupa Komisyonu'nun Mart 2026'da açıkladığı sanayi düzenlemesi taslağı, kamu alımları ve teşviklerde AB'de üretilen ürünlere öncelik verilmesini öngörüyor. İlk taslakta, Gümrük Birliği kapsamında Türkiye'de üretilen ürünlerin de Avrupa menşeli kabul edilmesine yönelik yaklaşım benimsenmişti. Ancak Fransa ve Almanya'nın 15-16 Ekim tarihlerinde vardığı uzlaşma, Türkiye'nin bu avantajı kaybedebileceği endişesini artırdı. Düzenlemenin Türkiye'yi dışarıda bırakacak şekilde yasalaşması halinde, Türkiye'de üretilen otomobiller ve sanayi parçaları Avrupa'daki bazı kamu destekleri ve teşviklerden yararlanamayabilir. Gümrük Birliği sorunu yeniden gündemde Yeni düzenlemeye ilişkin belirsizlikler, Türkiye ile AB arasındaki Gümrük Birliği'nin güncellenmesi ihtiyacını da yeniden gündeme taşıdı. Mevcut sistemde Türkiye, AB'nin üçüncü ülkelerle yaptığı ticaret anlaşmalarından kaynaklanan yükümlülüklerle karşılaşırken aynı ülkelerde eşdeğer ticari avantajlara otomatik olarak erişemiyor. Uzun süredir gündemde olan Gümrük Birliği'nin modernizasyonu konusunda ise henüz somut ilerleme sağlanamadı. Otomotiv ihracatında Avrupa'nın payı yüzde 73'ü aşıyor Türkiye açısından düzenlemenin önemi, otomotiv ihracatındaki Avrupa ağırlığından kaynaklanıyor. OİB verilerine göre otomotiv endüstrisi, ekim ayında 4 milyar 32 milyon dolarlık ihracatla aylık bazda tüm zamanların en yüksek seviyesine ulaştı. Sektörün ocak-ekim dönemindeki toplam ihracatı ise 35 milyar 174 milyon dolara ulaştı. Ekim ayında 650 milyon dolarlık ihracatla Almanya sektörün en büyük pazarı olurken, Fransa 475 milyon dolar ve Birleşik Krallık 396 milyon dolarla onu takip etti. Aynı dönemde AB ülkelerine yapılan otomotiv ihracatı 2 milyar 953 milyon dolara ulaşırken, birliğin toplam ihracattaki payı yüzde 73,2 olarak gerçekleşti. Türkiye'nin en büyük ihracat pazarlarından biri olan Almanya'da yapılacak görüşmelerde, yeni düzenlemenin Türk otomotiv sanayisinin Avrupa tedarik zincirindeki konumunu olumsuz etkilememesi için çözüm aranacak.

news.title: Government must act now or lose Royal Mail, former minister warns
news.summary: The former business secretary says "undercutting" by rivals will make Royal Mail "unviable".
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Government must act now or lose Royal Mail, former minister warns
news.summaryTr: The former business secretary says "undercutting" by rivals will make Royal Mail "unviable".
news.articleText: Government must act now or lose Royal Mail, former minister warns - Published Former Business Secretary Peter Kyle has said the government must act urgently to "level the playing field" for Royal Mail or risk the business becoming unviable. He said he was concerned that the firm was being "undercut" by rival parcel delivery firms who did not employ staff under the same conditions. Royal Mail, which is owned by International Distribution Services, has struggled in recent years with increased competition, fewer letters being sent and fines from the regulator for missing delivery targets. A government spokesperson said it would consider whether further reforms are required to the parcel market after the watchdog, Ofcom, publishes its annual monitoring report in December. Kyle had started to prepare officials at the Department for Business and Trade (DBT) to look at the delivery market for parcels shortly before he was replaced in his job by Jonathan Reynolds as business secretary in July. He said a "crunch point" had been reached where the government had to make a decision about whether it wants Royal Mail "to be a viable proposition in the future". He said his review would have looked at where the costs in that market lay and where the profit was being made, to see successful companies upheld "the values of business in Britain today". "If we leave it another few years then Royal Mail will just become unviable and it will just collapse under the weight of having full-time employees," he said. According to Royal Mail, 98% of its 130,000 workers are permanent employees, with rights to benefits including pensions, sick pay and holiday pay. Some other parcel delivery companies use self-employed delivery drivers, with some offering an opt-in service that gives couriers limited additional benefits. Royal Mail is also legally obliged to offer customers a "one price goes anywhere" service across the UK and to deliver first class letters six days a week to every address. Kyle's proposed review would not have considered further changes to Royal Mail's universal service obligations or to terms and conditions for its staff. Royal Mail's performance has improved in recent months but it is still missing its targets for delivering first and second class post. The firm was fined £21m in October 2025 for missing delivery targets in 2024/25. Ofcom agreed last year to scrap second class deliveries on Saturdays and to reduce the target for delivering first class post within a day of collection to 90%. A government spokesperson said the current business secretary had met Royal Mail and the Communication Workers Union, which represents postal workers, last week "to seek timely progress on improving their quality of service and to reiterate our commitment to the company's success." DBT has also launched a consultation on tackling, external what it calls "bogus" self-employment, which it describes as "a practice whereby some businesses mislabel staff as self-employed to avoid statutory obligations". Royal Mail has welcomed the consultation, and a spokesperson for the company claimed some parts of the delivery industry were "driving a race to the bottom" on employment standards and said it would "continue to push for a level playing field, with strong and enforceable standards across the industry." - Royal Mail misses delivery targets again but hails 'encouraging' signs - Published21 August - Hundreds of Royal Mail staff quitting each week under new efficiency plans - Published14 October Many MPs across the UK have reported receiving high volumes of complaints from constituents about missed and delayed deliveries. Shadow business minister Bradley Thomas said that Royal Mail's management needed to address the business's failings. "Customers are being asked time and time again to pay increased prices, yet the service they're receiving is not improving," he said. "Be in no doubt, this is not the fault of the hardworking postmen and women, it's the fault of Royal Mail's management. "Nationalisation isn't the solution to this problem. Instead, we need ministers and Ofcom to bear down on Royal Mail's management to ensure they deliver on the improvements they've promised their customers." The Communication Workers Union, which represents Royal Mail workers, is also putting pressure on ministers, with General Secretary Dave Ward calling for a "new model of ownership".

news.summaryTr: Venâncio Mondlane faces several charges over 2024 post-election protests that left hundreds of people dead.
news.articleText: Mozambique opposition leader faces trial over deadly 2024 election unrest - Published Tensions are running high in Mozambique's capital, Maputo, with a heavy police deployment as a prominent opposition leader goes on trial over deadly protests that followed the country's disputed 2024 elections. Venâncio Mondlane faces several charges, including incitement to terrorism and civil disobedience, over protests that left hundreds of people dead. He denies any wrongdoing. Security has been tightened around the Supreme Court, where Mondlane is due to appear on Tuesday, with authorities fearing a fresh wave of demonstrations by his supporters. Police have appealed to citizens to follow the proceedings calmly and avoid actions that could threaten public order. Mondlane arrived at the Supreme Court early on Tuesday with "great peace of mind", and was greeted by dozens of supporters. "As you can see, I arrive calm, confident in the work of my legal team," he told journalists gathered outside court, amid a heavy police presence. The trial is widely seen as a major test of Mozambique's political stability, nearly two years after disputed elections triggered some of the country's deadliest political unrest in decades. "The trial is a real test for Mozambique. It is is an important opportunity to demonstrate that the rule of law applies equally to everyone," said Luis Nhachote, a political analyst. Mondlane, who challenged the presidential election results that declared Daniel Chapo of the ruling Frelimo party the winner, accused the authorities of widespread electoral fraud and called for nationwide protests and work stoppages. - Children shot dead after joining pot-banging protests in Mozambique - Published23 November 2024 The demonstrations continued for months, with rights groups accusing security forces of using excessive force against protesters. Amnesty International, citing local civil society organisations, said more than 300 people were killed during the unrest, which was one of the country's worst post-election crises since independence. Mozambican police put the death toll at 96, including 17 police officers. European Union election observers also reported irregularities in the October 2024 vote, raising questions about the credibility of the results. Prosecutors accuse Mondlane of encouraging demonstrations that disrupted public services, damaged property and threatened public security. The charges include publicly glorifying criminal acts, incitement to collective disobedience, public instigation to commit crimes and offences linked to terrorism. He could face up to 24 years in prison if convicted of the most serious charge. Mondlane has rejected the accusations, insisting that his calls for demonstrations were aimed at demanding electoral transparency rather than encouraging violence. His party, the National Alliance for a Free and Autonomous Mozambique (Anamola), has described the prosecution as politically motivated. The Supreme Court has denied allegations of political interference in the proceedings. A heavy deployment of police has been seen patrolling around the Supreme Court and major streets in Maputo ahead of the trial. In a statement issued on Monday, Mozambique's police appealed to citizens to "preserve tolerance and peaceful coexistence," adding that the right to demonstrate must be exercised strictly within the limits of the law. Police also pledged to protect people and property while acting preventively and proportionately in accordance with the rule of law. The court has only granted access to selected media organisations, sparking criticism from journalists and press freedom campaigners. Court officials say the restrictions are necessary because of limited seating capacity in the courtroom, but critics argue they undermine transparency in a case of significant public interest. The proceedings are expected to be heard by five judges, with witnesses called by both the prosecution and defence. Political observers warn that the trial could reignite tensions in a country still struggling to recover from the violence and deep political divisions that followed the 2024 elections. news.title: Where are the most jobs for 18-24 year-olds?
news.summary: How many jobs are there where you live and in which sectors are you most likely to find an opening?
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Where are the most jobs for 18-24 year-olds?
news.summaryTr: How many jobs are there where you live and in which sectors are you most likely to find an opening?
news.articleText: Where are the most jobs for 18-24 year-olds? - Published If you're one of the nearly one million people aged 16-24 not in education, employment or training - otherwise known as "Neet" - then you might be wondering where to start. Under-25s should be guaranteed job placements or training to help them find permanent work, a major review aimed at cutting the number of Neets will say. But how many jobs are there where you live? Use our look-up tool to find out. Where are the available jobs? Where you live will often have a big impact on your ability to find a job. We have used online job adverts to help identify the number of vacancies suitable for young people in the area they live, relative to the size of the local population. The Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) think tank used AI to help identify the jobs, which were broadly defined as roles requiring relatively low experience or education. According to its analysis, South Oxfordshire had 387 suitable vacancies per 1,000 18 to 24-year-olds in the area - the most of any local authority. Rotherham had the least, at 53 per 1,000. Use this tool to check out the situation in your area. The data for London is only available for the region as a whole and is not broken down by individual councils. Which sectors have the most entry-level jobs? Even if there are jobs available in your area, you might not find one in the sector you want to work in. The sector with the highest average number of entry-level vacancies in the year to October was teaching, with most of those jobs being for teaching assistants, learning support and cover supervisor roles, according to jobs website Adzuna. The next largest was hospitality and catering, traditionally an area where younger people get their first experience of work. Adzuna, a major online jobs website, includes adverts for full-time roles marked as entry-level, those asking for up to two years' experience, graduate roles, internships and apprenticeships. Accounting and finance had the third-highest number of job openings. What are the typical rates of pay? Figures on salaries for vacancies can be patchy because many employers do not include them in job adverts. Prime Minister Andy Burnham recently urged businesses to start publishing salaries ahead of plans to make pay details compulsory in adverts. Only about 40% of Adzuna's jobs data for the year to October stated a salary, although that figure varies widely by sector. Here are the average salaries for jobs in the sectors with the largest number of entry-level jobs, according to Adzuna. The highest average salary is £30,530 in engineering, while social care has the lowest at £25,880. How many job vacancies are there overall? While it can be hard for anyone looking for their first job, the situation is also tough for older jobseekers. Across the whole economy there were 690,000 jobs available in the August to October period this year, which is the lowest number since early 2021. The Covid pandemic led to huge swings in the number of job vacancies available as companies reacted to shutdowns and then reopened as restrictions were lifted. Stripping out the fluctuations seen during the pandemic, the number of vacancies is now at its lowest level for 12 years. Apprenticeships have often been a way for people to get their first taste of employment. In England the number of people starting apprenticeships has risen in recent years, although this has been driven by an increase in those aged 25 and over after schemes for older workers were fully rolled out in 2008. The number of people aged 24 and under starting apprenticeships in England in 2025 was 172,230, down from a peak of 291,300 in 2012. news.title: Buzlar eridi, rekor geldi: Rusya'nın Arktik petrol rotasında hedef büyüdü
news.summary: Arktik bölgesinde eriyen buzullar Rusya'nın enerji taşımacılığı için yeni fırsatlar yaratırken Moskova kuzey deniz rotasındaki faaliyetlerini genişletiyor. Yaptırımların sürdüğü dönemde petrol sevkiyatını artıran Rusya'nın yeni projeleri ve kesintisiz taşımacılığa yönelik hazırlıkları gündeme geldi.

news.summaryTr: Arktik bölgesinde eriyen buzullar Rusya'nın enerji taşımacılığı için yeni fırsatlar yaratırken Moskova kuzey deniz rotasındaki faaliyetlerini genişletiyor. Yaptırımların sürdüğü dönemde petrol sevkiyatını artıran Rusya'nın yeni projeleri ve kesintisiz taşımacılığa yönelik hazırlıkları gündeme geldi.
news.articleText: Buzlar eridi, rekor geldi: Rusya'nın Arktik petrol rotasında hedef büyüdü - Arktik bölgesinde eriyen buzullar, Rusya'nın enerji taşımacılığı için yeni fırsatlar yaratırken Moskova kuzey deniz rotasındaki faaliyetlerini genişletiyor. - Yaptırımların sürdüğü dönemde petrol sevkiyatını artıran Rusya'nın yeni projeleri ve yıl boyunca kesintisiz taşımacılığa yönelik hazırlıkları gündeme geldi. Rusya'nın Kuzey Deniz Yolu üzerinden Asya'ya petrol sevkiyatı, Batılı ülkelerin yaptırımları ve geleneksel deniz yollarındaki güvenlik sorunlarının alternatif güzergahlara ilgiyi artırmasıyla bu yıl rekor seviyeye ulaşırken küresel ısınmanın etkisiyle buz örtüsünün azaldığı Arktik bölgesinin enerji ticaretindeki önemi artıyor. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Uluslararası enerji piyasaları araştırma kuruluşu S&P Global'in Commodities at Sea gemi takip verilerine göre, Rusya'nın Kuzey Deniz Yolu üzerinden Asya'ya ham petrol ve petrol ürünleri sevkiyatı, 2026'daki seyrüsefer sezonunda 13,2 milyon varile ulaştı. Sevkiyat miktarı 2024'te 10,8 milyon, 2025'te ise 12,2 milyon varil seviyesinde gerçekleşmişti. S&P Global'in 2 Kasım'da yayımladığı verilere göre, sevkiyatlar geçen yılın rekorunu yaklaşık yüzde 8 aşarken Rus petrol şirketi Rosneft'in Arktik bölgesindeki Vostok Oil projesinden gerçekleştirilen ilk sevkiyatlar da artışa katkı sağladı. Rusya'nın kuzey kıyıları boyunca uzanan Kuzey Deniz Yolu, Baltık Denizi'ndeki limanlardan hareket eden tankerler için Avrupa kıyıları ve Süveyş Kanalı üzerinden Asya'ya ulaşan geleneksel güzergaha alternatif oluşturuyor. Yaptırımlar Rus petrolünün yönünü değiştirdi Rusya'nın petrol ihracatındaki değişimde, Avrupa Birliği'nin (AB) Aralık 2022'de Rusya'dan deniz yoluyla ham petrol, Şubat 2023'te ise petrol ürünleri ithalatını yasaklaması önemli rol oynadı. Batılı ülkelerin Rus petrolüne yönelik tavan fiyat uygulaması ile deniz taşımacılığı, sigorta ve finansman hizmetlerine getirdiği kısıtlamalar, Rus enerji şirketlerinin ihracat pazarlarını ve lojistik güzergahlarını yeniden düzenlemesini hızlandırdı. Rusya Başbakan Yardımcısı Aleksandr Novak'ın ocakta "Enerji Politikası" dergisinde yayımlanan makalesine göre, ülkenin petrol ihracatında Asya ülkelerinin payı 2021'de yüzde 40 seviyesindeyken 2025'te yüzde 80'e yükseldi. Rusya'nın geçen yıl toplam 238 milyon ton petrol ihraç ettiğini bildiren Novak, Avrupa'ya yönelik sevkiyatın geçmişteki 175 milyon ton seviyesinden yaklaşık 25 milyon tona gerilediğini belirtti. AB Konseyinin temmuzda kabul ettiği 21'inci yaptırım paketi kapsamında, Rusya'nın petrol ticaretinde kullanılan 41 gemi daha yaptırım listesine eklenirken, kısıtlama uygulanan gemi sayısı 670'i aştı. Yaptırımların yanı sıra Kızıldeniz ve Hürmüz Boğazı çevresindeki güvenlik sorunları ile yükselen navlun fiyatları da kuzey rotasına ilgiyi artırdı. S&P Global'in araştırmasına göre, Rusya'nın batısındaki petrol terminallerinden Doğu Asya'ya Süveyş Kanalı üzerinden yapılan sevkiyatlar genellikle en az altı hafta sürüyor. Arktik güzergahında ise uygun buz koşullarında taşıma süresi yüzde 40'a kadar azalıyor. Kuzey rotasında mesafenin kısalması, yakıt tüketimi ve gemi kiralama giderleri açısından avantaj sağlarken buzkıran hizmetlerinin maliyeti, sınırlı sayıdaki uygun tanker ve zorlu iklim koşulları bu tasarrufu azaltıyor. Kuzey Deniz Yolu'nda 40 milyon tonluk taşımacılık beklentisi Rusya Devlet Nükleer Enerji Kuruluşu Rosatom Genel Müdürü Aleksey Lihaçev, 16 Ekim'de yaptığı açıklamada, Kuzey Deniz Yolu üzerinden gerçekleştirilen toplam yük taşımacılığının bu yıl 40 milyon tonu aşmasını beklediklerini bildirdi. Ekim ortası itibarıyla taşınan yük miktarının 35 milyon tonu geçtiğini belirten Lihaçev, bunun geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre yüzde 20 artış anlamına geldiğini kaydetti. Rusya Uzak Doğu ve Arktik Kalkınma Bakanı Aleksey Çekunkov da 11 Kasım'daki açıklamasında, güzergah üzerindeki transit taşımacılığın kasım başı itibarıyla 6 milyon tona ulaşarak geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre iki katına çıktığını belirtti. Rosatom verilerine göre, Kuzey Deniz Yolu üzerinden 2025'te toplam 37,2 milyon ton yük taşındı. Güzergah, petrol ve petrol ürünlerinin yanı sıra sıvılaştırılmış doğal gaz (LNG), maden cevheri ve konteyner taşımacılığında da kullanılıyor. Vostok Oil projesiyle petrol ihracatının artırılması hedefleniyor Rusya'nın Arktik bölgesindeki büyük enerji yatırımlarından Vostok Oil projesi kapsamında ilk petrol sevkiyatı, Devlet Başkanı Vladimir Putin'in katıldığı törenle eylülde yapıldı. Rosneft'in açıklamasına göre, Krasnoyarsk bölgesindeki petrol sahalarını Arktik kıyısındaki Buhta Sever Limanı'na bağlayan 790 kilometrelik petrol boru hattı devreye alınırken ilk petrol buz sınıfı Valentin Pikul tankerine yüklendi. Rosneft Üst Yöneticisi İgor Seçin, yıllık 100 milyon ton taşıma kapasitesine sahip olacak şekilde tasarlanan boru hattının bölgedeki petrolü uluslararası pazarlara ulaştıracağını belirtti. Rosatom'un Arktik Direktörü Vladimir Panov ise 27 Ekim'deki açıklamasında, proje kapsamında Kuzey Deniz Yolu üzerinden altı sevkiyat gerçekleştirildiğini bildirdi. Arktik'te buz örtüsü azalıyor Küresel ısınmanın etkisiyle Arktik bölgesindeki deniz buzlarının uzun vadede azalması, özellikle yaz ve sonbahar aylarında gemi taşımacılığına elverişli koşulların oluşmasına katkı sağlıyor. Rusya Federal Hidrometeoroloji ve Çevre İzleme Servisinin (Rosgidromet) 21 Eylül'de yayımladığı verilere göre, Arktik'teki deniz buzlarının kapladığı alan 16 Eylül itibarıyla 4,73 milyon kilometrekareye gerileyerek geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre yüzde 5 azaldı. Bununla birlikte, bölgede petrol taşımacılığının genişlemesi çevresel riskleri de gündeme getiriyor. S&P Global Maritime Intelligence Risk Suite verilerine göre, 2025-2026 döneminde Kuzey Deniz Yolu üzerinden uluslararası müşterilere Rus ham petrolü taşıyan 28 geminin tamamı, seferleri sırasında en az bir Batılı ülkenin yaptırım listesinde bulunuyordu. Gemilerin 7'sinin buz sınıfı kaydının bulunmaması, olası kazalar ve petrol sızıntılarına ilişkin endişeleri artırıyor. Rusya 2027'de yıl boyunca düzenli taşımacılık hedefliyor Rosatom'un Arktik Direktörü Panov, 27 Ekim'de İnterfaks haber ajansına verdiği röportajda, Kuzey Deniz Yolu üzerinden Asya yönündeki düzenli sevkiyatların 2027 başında yıl boyunca gerçekleştirilebilmesini hedeflediklerini bildirdi. Yeni nükleer buzkıran Çukotka'nın gelecek yılın başında hizmete alınmasının planlandığını belirten Panov, böylece Rusya'nın nükleer buzkıran filosundaki gemi sayısının 9'a yükseleceğini kaydetti. Rusya ile Çin arasında Kuzey Deniz Yolu'ndaki yük taşımacılığının 2030'a kadar yıllık 20 milyon tona çıkarılmasını öngören bir yol haritası da bulunuyor. Panov, düzenli taşımacılığın geliştirilmesi için gemilerin seyir hızının artırılması ve bölgedeki arama kurtarma, iletişim ve sağlık altyapısının güçlendirilmesi gerektiğini ifade etti.

Yaptırımlar Rus petrolünün yönünü değiştirdi Rusya'nın petrol ihracatındaki değişimde, Avrupa Birliği'nin (AB) Aralık 2022'de Rusya'dan deniz yoluyla ham petrol, Şubat 2023'te ise petrol ürünleri ithalatını yasaklaması önemli rol oynadı. Batılı ülkelerin Rus petrolüne yönelik tavan fiyat uygulaması ile deniz taşımacılığı, sigorta ve finansman hizmetlerine getirdiği kısıtlamalar, Rus enerji şirketlerinin ihracat pazarlarını ve lojistik güzergahlarını yeniden düzenlemesini hızlandırdı. Rusya Başbakan Yardımcısı Aleksandr Novak'ın ocakta "Enerji Politikası" dergisinde yayımlanan makalesine göre, ülkenin petrol ihracatında Asya ülkelerinin payı 2021'de yüzde 40 seviyesindeyken 2025'te yüzde 80'e yükseldi. Rusya'nın geçen yıl toplam 238 milyon ton petrol ihraç ettiğini bildiren Novak, Avrupa'ya yönelik sevkiyatın geçmişteki 175 milyon ton seviyesinden yaklaşık 25 milyon tona gerilediğini belirtti. AB Konseyinin temmuzda kabul ettiği 21'inci yaptırım paketi kapsamında, Rusya'nın petrol ticaretinde kullanılan 41 gemi daha yaptırım listesine eklenirken, kısıtlama uygulanan gemi sayısı 670'i aştı. Yaptırımların yanı sıra Kızıldeniz ve Hürmüz Boğazı çevresindeki güvenlik sorunları ile yükselen navlun fiyatları da kuzey rotasına ilgiyi artırdı. S&P Global'in araştırmasına göre, Rusya'nın batısındaki petrol terminallerinden Doğu Asya'ya Süveyş Kanalı üzerinden yapılan sevkiyatlar genellikle en az altı hafta sürüyor. Arktik güzergahında ise uygun buz koşullarında taşıma süresi yüzde 40'a kadar azalıyor. Kuzey rotasında mesafenin kısalması, yakıt tüketimi ve gemi kiralama giderleri açısından avantaj sağlarken buzkıran hizmetlerinin maliyeti, sınırlı sayıdaki uygun tanker ve zorlu iklim koşulları bu tasarrufu azaltıyor. Kuzey Deniz Yolu'nda 40 milyon tonluk taşımacılık beklentisi Rusya Devlet Nükleer Enerji Kuruluşu Rosatom Genel Müdürü Aleksey Lihaçev, 16 Ekim'de yaptığı açıklamada, Kuzey Deniz Yolu üzerinden gerçekleştirilen toplam yük taşımacılığının bu yıl 40 milyon tonu aşmasını beklediklerini bildirdi. Ekim ortası itibarıyla taşınan yük miktarının 35 milyon tonu geçtiğini belirten Lihaçev, bunun geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre yüzde 20 artış anlamına geldiğini kaydetti. Rusya Uzak Doğu ve Arktik Kalkınma Bakanı Aleksey Çekunkov da 11 Kasım'daki açıklamasında, güzergah üzerindeki transit taşımacılığın kasım başı itibarıyla 6 milyon tona ulaşarak geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre iki katına çıktığını belirtti. Rosatom verilerine göre, Kuzey Deniz Yolu üzerinden 2025'te toplam 37,2 milyon ton yük taşındı. Güzergah, petrol ve petrol ürünlerinin yanı sıra sıvılaştırılmış doğal gaz (LNG), maden cevheri ve konteyner taşımacılığında da kullanılıyor. Vostok Oil projesiyle petrol ihracatının artırılması hedefleniyor Rusya'nın Arktik bölgesindeki büyük enerji yatırımlarından Vostok Oil projesi kapsamında ilk petrol sevkiyatı, Devlet Başkanı Vladimir Putin'in katıldığı törenle eylülde yapıldı. Rosneft'in açıklamasına göre, Krasnoyarsk bölgesindeki petrol sahalarını Arktik kıyısındaki Buhta Sever Limanı'na bağlayan 790 kilometrelik petrol boru hattı devreye alınırken ilk petrol buz sınıfı Valentin Pikul tankerine yüklendi. Rosneft Üst Yöneticisi İgor Seçin, yıllık 100 milyon ton taşıma kapasitesine sahip olacak şekilde tasarlanan boru hattının bölgedeki petrolü uluslararası pazarlara ulaştıracağını belirtti. Rosatom'un Arktik Direktörü Vladimir Panov ise 27 Ekim'deki açıklamasında, proje kapsamında Kuzey Deniz Yolu üzerinden altı sevkiyat gerçekleştirildiğini bildirdi. Arktik'te buz örtüsü azalıyor Küresel ısınmanın etkisiyle Arktik bölgesindeki deniz buzlarının uzun vadede azalması, özellikle yaz ve sonbahar aylarında gemi taşımacılığına elverişli koşulların oluşmasına katkı sağlıyor. Rusya Federal Hidrometeoroloji ve Çevre İzleme Servisinin (Rosgidromet) 21 Eylül'de yayımladığı verilere göre, Arktik'teki deniz buzlarının kapladığı alan 16 Eylül itibarıyla 4,73 milyon kilometrekareye gerileyerek geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre yüzde 5 azaldı. Bununla birlikte, bölgede petrol taşımacılığının genişlemesi çevresel riskleri de gündeme getiriyor. S&P Global Maritime Intelligence Risk Suite verilerine göre, 2025-2026 döneminde Kuzey Deniz Yolu üzerinden uluslararası müşterilere Rus ham petrolü taşıyan 28 geminin tamamı, seferleri sırasında en az bir Batılı ülkenin yaptırım listesinde bulunuyordu. Gemilerin 7'sinin buz sınıfı kaydının bulunmaması, olası kazalar ve petrol sızıntılarına ilişkin endişeleri artırıyor. Rusya 2027'de yıl boyunca düzenli taşımacılık hedefliyor Rosatom'un Arktik Direktörü Panov, 27 Ekim'de İnterfaks haber ajansına verdiği röportajda, Kuzey Deniz Yolu üzerinden Asya yönündeki düzenli sevkiyatların 2027 başında yıl boyunca gerçekleştirilebilmesini hedeflediklerini bildirdi. Yeni nükleer buzkıran Çukotka'nın gelecek yılın başında hizmete alınmasının planlandığını belirten Panov, böylece Rusya'nın nükleer buzkıran filosundaki gemi sayısının 9'a yükseleceğini kaydetti. Rusya ile Çin arasında Kuzey Deniz Yolu'ndaki yük taşımacılığının 2030'a kadar yıllık 20 milyon tona çıkarılmasını öngören bir yol haritası da bulunuyor. Panov, düzenli taşımacılığın geliştirilmesi için gemilerin seyir hızının artırılması ve bölgedeki arama kurtarma, iletişim ve sağlık altyapısının güçlendirilmesi gerektiğini ifade etti.

items.title: Bitcoin to $1M by 2030? ‘Almost certainly not,’ says Dragonfly’s Qureshi
items.summary: Dragonfly’s Haseeb Qureshi says Bitcoin could reach $400,000 by 2030 but doubts it will return to $100,000 by year-end with the rout in AI stocks weighing on crypto.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Bitcoin to $1M by 2030? ‘Almost certainly not,’ says Dragonfly’s Qureshi
items.summaryTr: Dragonfly’s Haseeb Qureshi says Bitcoin could reach $400,000 by 2030 but doubts it will return to $100,000 by year-end with the rout in AI stocks weighing on crypto.
items.articleText: Bitcoin to $1M by 2030? ‘Almost certainly not,’ says Dragonfly’s Qureshi Dragonfly’s Haseeb Qureshi says Bitcoin could reach $400,000 by 2030 but doubts it will return to $100,000 by year-end with the rout in AI stocks weighing on crypto. Bitcoin is unlikely to reach $1 million by 2030 — though it could reach $400,000 — according to Dragonfly managing partner Haseeb Qureshi. “The amount of capital that would have to come into crypto to get to million-dollar Bitcoin is an astronomical sum,” Qureshi tells Cointelegraph’s Trade Secrets. “The idea that you could get that amount of capital in five years or four years is just not plausible.” A former professional poker player and software engineer at Airbnb, Qureshi now backs crypto startups at Dragonfly, which launched a $650 million fund in February. Qureshi also says he doubts Bitcoin will return to six figures by year-end, linking the current crypto sell-off to the rout in AI stocks. AI sell-off spills into Bitcoin Nvidia (NVDA) shares closed 4.3% lower on Thursday after the chipmaker announced co-founder Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO following a series of scandals. Huang reportedly had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. Beijing denied the espionage allegation and President Donald Trump has expressed doubts too. Nvidia is the leading AI chip supplier and accounted for 4.66% of the MSCI All Country World Index at the end of October, second only to Apple. Bitcoin fell alongside Nvidia shares in the week Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO. Source: TradingView “Crypto is not the main story this year for financial markets,” Qureshi says. “Crypto is downstream of these other stories.” Qureshi says investors grew concerned after Democrat sweep in the US midterms that new data centers would be harder to get approved. With high oil prices and inflation already weighing on the economy, the prospect of weaker AI investment prompted investors to cut exposure to riskier assets, including Bitcoin, he says. Related: Jensen Huang weighs Nvidia comeback days after shock exit: FT That leaves crypto “largely along for the ride” through the year-end. Crypto has spent much of 2026 in a bear market despite Bitcoin’s 43% recovery in the third quarter. Bitcoin traded near $65,000 on Monday, almost 50% below its October 2025 all-time high. Bitcoin is far away from its $126,080 all-time high recorded in October 2025. Source: CoinGecko The US Senate failed to advance the CLARITY Act in September, stalling the industry’s push for federal rules for crypto markets. In October, suspected North Korean hackers stole about $6.3 billion from Binance in the largest crypto theft on record. Digital gold as a rival to actual gold Over the next 15 to 20 years, Qureshi says Bitcoin could compete with gold as a store of value outside government control. New deposits or advances in mining could add to the supply of gold, he says while Bitcoin’s protocol caps its supply at 21 million units. “There will never be an asteroid that you will find a bunch of Bitcoin on.” However, Qureshi sees a risk that AI could discover a flaw in the mathematics that secures Bitcoin transactions. Bitcoin uses digital signatures to verify that a transaction was signed with the corresponding private key. If a future mathematical breakthrough makes it possible to forge those signatures, attackers could move coins without their owners’ permission. Such a threat is often discussed alongside quantum computing risks. A powerful quantum computer could derive a private key from its corresponding public key using Shor’s algorithim, putting coins with public keys visible at risk of theft, which includes some of Satoshi Nakamoto’s early holdings. Related: Nearly 10% of Bitcoin supply is ‘structurally unsafe’ from quantum breakthrough: Glassnode In October, OpenAI said one of its models had found a faster way to solve certain logic problems, challenging a conjecture known as the Exponential Time Hypothesis. Qureshi says a future AI-assisted discovery could break the cryptography Bitcoin uses to verify who can spend coins, undermining its case as a store of value. “That, I think, is what you should price in as the chance this all breaks, this all fails,” he says. Dragonfly’s bets on stablecoins and AI Dragonfly has a history of backing innovative projects, and led stablecoin project Ethena’s $6 million seed round in 2023. Ethena had about $4.9 billion of its dollar-linked USDe token outstanding at the end of September. The protocol uses derivatives to offset price swings in the assets backing USDe. Some of the income those positions generate goes to users who stake the token. Dragonfly also led a $65 million funding round for the privacy focused AI firm Venice in July. The startup said it had 3.5 million registered users and put its valuation at $1 billion. Venice says it keeps chat histories on users’ devices and lets them choose among models with different privacy settings. Users who stake Venice’s VVV token can mint DIEM, which they can stake for daily credits to run AI models. Qureshi says demand for services like Venice could grow as users look for more privacy and fewer restrictions on what they can ask. Hodler’s Digest: US sellers drive Bitcoin crash, Jensen plots Nvidia comeback

items.articleText: Çin gerilimi Nvidia'nın yönetimine taşındı: Kritik komite kuruldu - Nvidia, ulusal güvenlik ve ihracat kontrollerini denetlemek amacıyla yönetim kurulu bünyesinde yeni bir komite kuruyor. - Şirketin adımı, Çin bağlantılı casusluk iddiaları etrafında gündeme gelen jeopolitik tartışmaların ardından geldi. ABD'li çip üreticisi Nvidia, ulusal güvenlik politikaları ve ihracat kontrollerine uyumu yakından izlemek için yönetim kurulu bünyesinde yeni bir komite oluşturuyor. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Şirketin açıklamasına göre Ulusal Güvenlik ve İhracat Kontrolü Denetim Komitesi, ulusal güvenlik politikalarını, ihracat kontrollerine uyumu ve küresel ticaretten kaynaklanan riskleri denetleyecek. Komiteye yönetim kurulu üyesi Suzanne Nora Johnson başkanlık edecek. Komite, en az üç ayda bir toplanarak ilgili konuları değerlendirecek. Çin bağlantılı iddiaların ardından geldi Nvidia'nın bu adımı, şirketin eski CEO'su Jensen Huang hakkında gündeme gelen ve Çin bağlantılı casusluk şüphesi bulunan bir kişiyle yaşadığı iddia edilen evlilik dışı ilişkiye ilişkin jeopolitik tartışmaların ardından geldi. Yeni komitenin kurulması, şirketin ulusal güvenlik ve ihracat kontrolü süreçlerine yönelik yönetim kurulu denetimini güçlendirme adımlarından biri olarak öne çıkıyor.

items.articleText: Rusya'dan akaryakıt arzı için rafinerilere onarım talimatı - Rusya Başbakan Yardımcısı Aleksandr Novak, iç piyasada akaryakıt arzının istikrarlı sürdürülmesi için rafinerilerdeki onarımların hızlandırılmasını ve petrol ürünleri ithalatına devam edilmesini istedi. Ülkede Ukrayna'nın saldırıları nedeniyle rafinerilerde üretim aksaklıkları yaşanıyor. Rusya Başbakan Yardımcısı Aleksandr Novak, iç piyasada akaryakıt arzının istikrarlı şekilde sürdürülmesi için petrol rafinerilerindeki onarımların hızlandırılmasını ve petrol ürünleri ithalatına devam edilmesini istedi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Rus hükümetinden yapılan yazılı açıklamada, Novak'ın ilgili bakanlıklar, kamu kurumları ve petrol şirketlerinin temsilcileriyle akaryakıt piyasasındaki gelişmeleri değerlendirdiği belirtildi. Rusya'da akaryakıt arzı için rafineri onarımları hızlandırılıyor Novak'ın öncelikleri arasında petrol rafinerilerinin üretim kapasitelerinin en kısa sürede yeniden devreye alınması ve Euro-5 çevre standardını karşılamayan akaryakıtın ilave miktarlarda piyasaya sunulmasının bulunduğu bildirildi. Açıklamada, Novak'ın petrol ürünleri ithalatına yönelik çalışmaların sürdürülmesini istediği, ilgili kurumlar ve şirketlere de iç talebin karşılanması için azami çaba gösterilmesi talimatını verdiği kaydedildi. Toplantıda, büyük petrol şirketlerinin akaryakıt arzını istikrarlı tutmak için aldığı ek önlemler, şirketlere ait akaryakıt istasyonları ile bağımsız işletmelere yapılan sevkiyatlar ve tarım üreticilerinin yakıt ihtiyaçları da ele alındı. Ukrayna'nın Rusya'daki petrol rafinerilerine yönelik insansız hava aracı saldırıları nedeniyle ülkede çok sayıda tesisin üretimi aksarken hükümet, iç piyasadaki arz sorunlarını hafifletmek amacıyla akaryakıt ihracatına kısıtlamalar uyguluyor.

items.titleTr: ARK sells $85M in Nvidia shares ahead of chipmaker’s Q3 earnings results
items.summaryTr: ARK bought shares in Block, Circle and Coinbase worth about $39.9 million at Monday’s close while selling Nvidia and Solana and Ether staking ETFs.
items.articleText: ARK sells $85M in Nvidia shares ahead of chipmaker’s Q3 earnings results ARK bought shares in Block, Circle and Coinbase worth about $39.9 million at Monday’s close while selling Nvidia and Solana and Ether staking ETFs. Funds managed by Cathie Wood’s ARK Investment Management bought shares in Block, Circle and Coinbase worth about $39.9 million at Monday’s closing prices, while selling Nvidia shares and Solana and Ether staking ETFs. ARK sold 543,092 Nvidia (NVDA) shares worth approximately $84.8 million and about 30,659 Bullish (BLSH) shares valued at about $605,000. The company also sold about 350,000 shares of 3iQ Solana Staking ETF and 300,000 shares of the 3iQ Ether Staking ETF, according to its Monday trade disclosure. The funds bought 277,523 Block shares, 180,534 Circle shares and 53,760 Coinbase shares, according to ARK’s Monday trade disclosure. Those purchases were valued at approximately $23 million, $10.4 million and $6.4 million, respectively, using closing prices. ARK also bought 378,515 SpaceX shares, valued at about $52 million. ARK’s Nvidia sale comes ahead of the chipmaker’s third-quarter earnings results scheduled for publication after market close on Tuesday, which are expected to test whether AI infrastructure spending can justify Nvidia’s growth expectations. Nvidia earnings follow leadership change Nvidia’s stock fell 4% on Monday to close at $156, extending its year-to-date decline to over 16%, according to Yahoo Finance data. Nvidia’s shares declined after its board members reportedly ruled out co-founder Jensen Huang’s return as CEO. Related: Jensen Huang weighs Nvidia comeback days after shock exit: FT Huang resigned last week following reports of extramarital affairs, one of which was with an alleged Chinese spy, with chief financial officer Colette Kress taking over as interim CEO. S&P Global Market Intelligence analyst Melissa Otto said the key question is whether the earnings release can provide the “next positive catalyst for the stock or are expectations largely priced in for now,” according to a Thursday report. The analyst expects Nvidia to report third-quarter revenue of about $109.3 billion, led by $101.8 billion from its data center business. Nvidia year-to-date chart. Source: Yahoo Finance Magazine: US sellers drive Bitcoin crash, Jensen plots Nvidia comeback: Hodler’s Digest

items.title: Speed camera fault may have allowed drivers to escape fines
items.summary: The Home Office has revoked approval that allowed footage from speed cameras to be used in evidence.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Speed camera fault may have allowed drivers to escape fines
items.summaryTr: The Home Office has revoked approval that allowed footage from speed cameras to be used in evidence.
items.articleText: Speed camera fault may have allowed drivers to escape fines - Published Further problems with the accuracy of speed cameras on English roads have been uncovered which may have allowed drivers to slip through the cracks and escape fines. National Highways discovered issues with speed cameras last year, affecting 154 out of 400 cameras but, following an investigation, said it had found another fault on units monitoring roads including those running between Huntingdon and Cambridge. The Home Office has revoked approval that allows footage from the cameras to be used as evidence in legal proceedings. US firm Verra Mobility operates the cameras but National Highways said it will now end the contract. Roads minister Justin Madders said: "We can't take chances with this. "If we're going to prosecute people, we need to be confident the system is working as it should. That's why we've taken the action we have." The fault affected all of the variable speed cameras on smart motorways, and a section of the A14 between Huntingdon and Cambridge as well as the A1 approach junction to the A14. A spokesperson for National Highways said that Verra's camera system had been selected on the basis that it maintained Home Office approval. The agency said that since that was no longer the case "we are ending our contractual relationship to use the cameras for enforcement". It added: "We are considering all further commercial and legal options that may be appropriate." The BBC has contacted Verra Mobility for comment. Madders said that the enforcement of speed limits continues to be conducted through a range of different tactics, including mobile cameras as well as marked and unmarked police patrols. But he admitted that the camera system will not be fully fixed until sometime next year. There are 4,000 cameras across the entire road network. In December 2025, National Highways, which runs England's motorways, blamed an "anomaly" in how variable speed cameras were interacting with speed limit signs on some A roads and motorways. For example, on a road where the speed limit increases, a driver may see a sign showing 60mph but the camera recording it may still be working on the basis of a previous 40mph speed limit. The fault led to 2,650 wrongful speed camera activations between 2021 and the end of last year. Those who had been wrongfully fined have been reimbursed. As National Highways continued to test the system, it discovered a further problem "relating to how some of these cameras may activate in specific and rare circumstances". It said that according to its calculations, "the circumstances in which the latest issue could occur are extremely rare, and there is no evidence to suggest it has impacted enforcement". Nevertheless, it said it was "taking immediate steps to ensure compliance is maintained at relevant locations". It said it would out further traffic officer patrols in place to monitor the sites. - Published16 December 2025 - Published12 February

items.title: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says
items.summary: Palestinians say there was an attack by settlers in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, while the Israeli military says the settlers fired after being attacked.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says
items.summaryTr: Palestinians say there was an attack by settlers in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, while the Israeli military says the settlers fired after being attacked.
items.articleText: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says - Published A Palestinian woman in her 70s has been shot dead, and several other people wounded, in a village in the occupied West Bank where Israeli settlers recently moved in, the Palestinian health ministry says. There are conflicting accounts of what happened. Local Palestinians said there was an attack by settlers in part of al-Duyuk al-Tahta, near Jericho, which is meant to be under the full control of the Palestinian Authority. According to the Israeli army, there was a Palestinian car-ramming attack on an Israeli vehicle. It said rocks were then thrown at the Israelis, who opened fire in response. There have been high tensions in the area since a group of settlers recently set up a new outpost. They moved into eight houses in the village on 4 November after buying them, they have said, in a secretive operation. The properties are in an area where Israel retains full security control. All settlements are illegal under international law. Palestinian reports said Fadwa al-Fahidat, who was 72, was shot outside her home on Monday evening and that, hearing the news, her son sped to the scene in his car. He then collided with an empty Israeli vehicle parked outside his family home and settlers standing nearby were injured, they said. The settlers then began shooting, the reports said. The statement from the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said that "terrorists accelerated their vehicle toward an Israeli vehicle and rammed it", and then "exited their vehicle with weapons and attacked and harmed the occupants of the Israeli vehicle". Afterwards, it said, "rocks were hurled at the Israelis, who responded by firing in order to remove the threat." It did not mention the fatal shooting of a woman. The IDF said that Israeli security forces were sent to the scene and were pursuing suspects. Doctors at a hospital in Jericho said that al-Fahidat was shot in the head. Several other Palestinians and Israelis were injured, reports said. The Israeli human rights group B'Tselem says there has been a prolonged campaign of settler attacks, intimidation and land seizures in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, with Israeli troops now stationed nearby to secure the new settlement. Residents and activists say armed settlers walk and drive quad bikes around the neighbourhood as they threaten Palestinian residents. In a separate incident on Monday evening, eight Palestinians were injured when they were hit by a vehicle driven by an Israeli settler on a main road in Tuqu, south of Bethlehem, according to Palestinian officials and the Palestinian Red Crescent. The IDF said the incident was a traffic accident. But the Palestinian foreign ministry called it a "terrorist attack", saying the driver hit a group of Palestinians who had gathered near the scene of an earlier traffic accident. Also on Monday, the Civil Administration - the body that implements Israeli government policy in the West Bank - announced the allocation of more than 28 sq km (6,945 acres) of land in the northern Jordan Valley to nine settlers for grazing, according to the Israeli anti-settlement watchdog Peace Now. It said handing over vast tracts of land to settlers for grazing outposts constituted "direct support for the systematic expulsion of Palestinians from their lands and the rampant criminal violence in the West Bank". The UK government said on Tuesday that it was imposing sanctions on eight companies building Israeli settlements in the West Bank. It is the first sanctions package since Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband's pledge in September to respond to the accelerating rate of settlement expansion in the West Bank, which he said risked rendering a two-state solution unviable. items.summaryTr: Walt Disney, 2029'a kadar yıllık maliyetlerini 3 milyar dolar azaltmayı hedefliyor. Kârlılığını artırmak isteyen şirket, işten çıkarmalar ve gider kesintileriyle yeniden yapılanmaya giderken Pixar, ABC News ve ESPN de bu süreçten etkilendi.
items.articleText: Disney'den 3 milyar dolarlık tasarruf planı: İşten çıkarmalar sürüyor - Walt Disney, 2029'a kadar yıllık maliyetlerini 3 milyar dolar azaltmayı hedefliyor. - Kârlılığını artırmak isteyen şirket, işten çıkarmalar ve gider kesintileriyle yeniden yapılanmaya giderken Pixar, ABC News ve ESPN de bu süreçten etkilendi. Eğlence devi Walt Disney, maliyetlerini düşürerek kârlılığını artırmak için kapsamlı bir tasarruf planı yürütüyor. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Şirket, 2029 yılına kadar yıllık giderlerini 3 milyar dolar azaltmayı hedefliyor. Plan kapsamında işten çıkarmaların yanı sıra farklı kalemlerde harcama kesintilerine gidiliyor. Disney, Hollywood'daki diğer büyük stüdyolar gibi yayın akışı sektöründe 2022'de yaşanan büyüme döneminin sona ermesinin ardından iş modelini yeniden şekillendirmeye çalışıyor. Şirket, eğlence faaliyetlerini büyütürken kârlılığını koruyabileceğini yatırımcılara göstermeyi amaçlıyor. Hollywood devlerinde tasarruf yarışı Sektördeki maliyet azaltma adımları Disney ile sınırlı değil. Netflix, geçen ay yaklaşık 1.000 çalışanını işten çıkarırken film ve televizyon bölümlerinden sorumlu üst düzey yöneticilerle de yollarını ayırdı. Paramount ve Warner Bros. stüdyolarının sahibi Skydance ise çalışanlarına gönüllü ayrılma paketleri sunarak personel sayısını azaltmayı planlıyor. Şirketin yeniden yapılanma kapsamında 6 milyar dolarlık tasarruf hedeflediği belirtiliyor. Disney'de daha az çalışanla daha fazla iş hedefi Disney CEO'su Josh D'Amaro, mart ayında Bob Iger'den görevi devralmasından bu yana şirketin operasyonlarını sadeleştirmeye odaklandı. D'Amaro'nun üst düzey yöneticilerden daha az personelle daha fazla iş üretmelerini istediği belirtiliyor. Yeniden yapılanma ve personel azaltma adımları şimdiye kadar Pixar'ın animasyon birimini, ABC News'u ve ESPN'i etkiledi. Hollywood'daki büyük eğlence şirketleri, yayın akışı sektöründe büyüme odaklı yatırımların ardından kârlılığı önceliklendiren yeni bir döneme girdi. İşten çıkarmalar ve maliyet azaltma programları, sektördeki dönüşümün önemli başlıkları arasında yer alıyor.

items.titleTr: Putin's Crimea bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
items.summaryTr: Ukraine says the attack took weeks to plan, while the Kremlin vows to rebuild the strategic bridge.
items.articleText: Putin's Crimea bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine - Published Ukraine has severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, in what Volodymyr Zelensky says was an "unprecedented operation" weeks in the making. Images shared by Ukrainian officials show a section of the Crimean Bridge - also known as the Kerch Bridge - has collapsed into the water, dealing a logistical and symbolic blow to Russia's war effort. The Kremlin said it would rebuild the bridge "better than before" and that Russian President Vladimir Putin had been briefed on the attack, though he is yet to comment. Elsewhere, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the Northern and Southern bridges, both important crossings over the Dnipro River, were closed after Russia targeted the Ukrainian capital overnight. Ukraine has long targeted the Crimean Bridge, which provides a road and rail route for Russian soldiers heading towards the front line, but has struggled to close it for good. The damage reported on Tuesday appeared to be far more severe than previously, with a large arched section of the bridge apparently destroyed. Video footage appeared to show critical damage to the road section, with remnants of the support arch and road deck seen protruding from the water below. Zelensky said the overnight strike was the result of a seven-stage operation by the military and security services, which saw Ukrainian forces "gradually destroy air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment, and other designated targets on the way to the final objective". He said the rail section parallel to the bridge's road had also been hit by a wave of drones, though images showed its supporting arch was still standing and a Russian-backed official said some rail services were operating. The Security Service of Ukraine said operations had "systematically suppressed enemy air defence systems" over a month, and said it showed "no Russian defence systems can guarantee the safety of illegal objects occupied by the invaders". The bridge was built by Russia after it invaded and annexed the peninsula in 2014, and was personally opened by Putin in 2018. While Ukraine has been trying to increase the cost to Russia of waging war economically, by hitting oil refineries and depots, striking the bridge is an attempt to increase the political cost on Putin. The timing of the strike comes at a significant moment, ahead of Putin meeting the leaders of China and the US. This could cloud his moment back in the spotlight. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge would "be restored following Ukrainian strikes, and it will be even better than before", and did not rule out the possibility the strikes were linked to Putin's visit to China. Russia's Investigative Committee confirmed structural damage and said it had opened a "criminal case... on terrorism charges" after attacks by "Ukraine's armed formations". For the second day in a row, Russia recorded the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, with 2,256 drones downed, according to the defence ministry. Zelensky had warned of major attacks in the days leading up to a meeting between Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in China's Shenzhen on Thursday. Loud explosions were heard in Kyiv just before midnight on Tuesday, with Klitschko saying shortly after that the city had suffered "damage to critical infrastructure systems" and disruption to heating and water. Some of Kyiv's above-ground subway services were damaged in the overnight attacks, officials said, after civilians were told to go to civil defence shelters. Eight major bridges span the Dnipro River connecting the western and eastern parts of Kyiv, and an estimated three million residents rely on the bridges to travel across the city. Strikes on the busy Northern and Southern Bridges will cause major disruption to people's daily lives. Elsewhere, three people have been injured in a Russian missile attack in the Cherkasy region, according to local officials. The long-term impact of the Crimean Bridge strike is still not fully clear though the risk of a serious transport and logistics crisis for the Russian military has increased significantly. The collapse of the arched section of the Crimean Bridge has cut off the peninsula's direct road and rail links with Russia – at least until the crossing can be repaired. However, there is still a land corridor running through the occupied parts of the Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions - though Ukraine has been systematically striking transport routes across northern Crimea, as well as bridges and other crossings in the area around Chongar. This has already caused problems with the delivery of fuel and other supplies, including military cargo. There is a ferry crossing across the Kerch Strait. It could partly compensate for the loss of the bridge, but its capacity is very limited and it is also vulnerable to attack. Russia could also supply Crimea by sea, but this route is also risky, as Ukrainian naval and aerial drones operate extensively in the area. In addition, debris from the Crimean Bridge – particularly its enormous arch – may have blocked the shipping channel. This would make it harder for larger vessels to pass through and create further problems for ports in the Sea of Azov, including Mariupol and Berdiansk. Russia's launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine is now under Russian occupation and Kyiv has refused Putin's demand to give up areas of Ukraine's eastern Donbas that remain under its control. items.summaryTr: Cezayir'in Arzew Limanı'ndan 15 Kasım'da ayrılan 144 bin 888 metreküp kapasiteli LNG gemisi Lalla Fatma N'Soumer'in, 20 Kasım'da Aliağa LNG Terminali'ne yanaşması bekleniyor.
items.articleText: Cezayir'den Türkiye'ye LNG sevkiyatı: Varış tarihi belli oldu YAYIN TARİHİ, 17 Kasım 2026 15:58 PAYLAŞ - Cezayir'in Arzew Limanı'ndan 15 Kasım'da ayrılan 144 bin 888 metreküp kapasiteli LNG gemisi Lalla Fatma N'Soumer'in, 20 Kasım'da Aliağa LNG Terminali'ne yanaşması bekleniyor. Cezayir'in Arzew Limanı'ndan yola çıkan "Lalla Fatma N'Soumer" adlı LNG gemisinin 20 Kasım'da Türkiye'de olması bekleniyor. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Uluslararası gemi takip verilerinden derlenen bilgilere göre, 15 Kasım'da Arzew Limanı'ndan ayrılan gemi, Malta adası açıklarında seyrine devam ediyor. Toplam 144 bin 888 metreküp kapasiteli geminin, 20 Kasım'da Aliağa LNG Terminali'ne yanaşması planlanıyor. Bahamalar bayraklı gemi 2004'te inşa edilmişti. Kaynak: AA

items.articleText: Otomotivciler Almanya yolunda: Bakan Bolat'tan 'Made in EU' hamlesi - Avrupa Birliği'nin 'Made in EU' düzenlemesinde Türkiye'nin kapsam dışında kalma ihtimali otomotiv sektörünü harekete geçirdi. Ticaret Bakanı Ömer Bolat, sektör temsilcileriyle birlikte kritik görüşmeler için Almanya'ya gidiyor. Avrupa Birliği'nin (AB) sanayisini korumaya yönelik yeni düzenleme hazırlıkları, Türkiye'nin en önemli ihracat sektörlerinden otomotivde endişe yarattı. Bazı Avrupa ülkelerinin Türkiye'de üretilen ürünleri "Made in EU" kapsamı dışında tutmaya yönelik girişimleri üzerine Ankara ve otomotiv sektörü diplomasi trafiğini hızlandırdı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Ticaret Bakanı Ömer Bolat'ın öncülüğünde, Uludağ Otomotiv Endüstrisi İhracatçıları Birliği (OİB) ve önde gelen otomotiv üreticilerinin temsilcilerinden oluşan heyet, perşembe günü Almanya'ya gidecek. Heyetin, Almanya Ekonomi ve Enerji Bakanı Katherina Reiche ile Türkiye'de yatırımları bulunan büyük otomotiv şirketlerinin yöneticileriyle bir araya gelmesi planlanıyor. Türkiye'nin kapsam dışında kalma riski Avrupa Komisyonu'nun Mart 2026'da açıkladığı sanayi düzenlemesi taslağı, kamu alımları ve teşviklerde AB'de üretilen ürünlere öncelik verilmesini öngörüyor. İlk taslakta, Gümrük Birliği kapsamında Türkiye'de üretilen ürünlerin de Avrupa menşeli kabul edilmesine yönelik yaklaşım benimsenmişti. Ancak Fransa ve Almanya'nın 15-16 Ekim tarihlerinde vardığı uzlaşma, Türkiye'nin bu avantajı kaybedebileceği endişesini artırdı. Düzenlemenin Türkiye'yi dışarıda bırakacak şekilde yasalaşması halinde, Türkiye'de üretilen otomobiller ve sanayi parçaları Avrupa'daki bazı kamu destekleri ve teşviklerden yararlanamayabilir. Gümrük Birliği sorunu yeniden gündemde Yeni düzenlemeye ilişkin belirsizlikler, Türkiye ile AB arasındaki Gümrük Birliği'nin güncellenmesi ihtiyacını da yeniden gündeme taşıdı. Mevcut sistemde Türkiye, AB'nin üçüncü ülkelerle yaptığı ticaret anlaşmalarından kaynaklanan yükümlülüklerle karşılaşırken aynı ülkelerde eşdeğer ticari avantajlara otomatik olarak erişemiyor. Uzun süredir gündemde olan Gümrük Birliği'nin modernizasyonu konusunda ise henüz somut ilerleme sağlanamadı. Otomotiv ihracatında Avrupa'nın payı yüzde 73'ü aşıyor Türkiye açısından düzenlemenin önemi, otomotiv ihracatındaki Avrupa ağırlığından kaynaklanıyor. OİB verilerine göre otomotiv endüstrisi, ekim ayında 4 milyar 32 milyon dolarlık ihracatla aylık bazda tüm zamanların en yüksek seviyesine ulaştı. Sektörün ocak-ekim dönemindeki toplam ihracatı ise 35 milyar 174 milyon dolara ulaştı. Ekim ayında 650 milyon dolarlık ihracatla Almanya sektörün en büyük pazarı olurken, Fransa 475 milyon dolar ve Birleşik Krallık 396 milyon dolarla onu takip etti. Aynı dönemde AB ülkelerine yapılan otomotiv ihracatı 2 milyar 953 milyon dolara ulaşırken, birliğin toplam ihracattaki payı yüzde 73,2 olarak gerçekleşti. Türkiye'nin en büyük ihracat pazarlarından biri olan Almanya'da yapılacak görüşmelerde, yeni düzenlemenin Türk otomotiv sanayisinin Avrupa tedarik zincirindeki konumunu olumsuz etkilememesi için çözüm aranacak.
items.articleTextTr: Otomotivciler Almanya yolunda: Bakan Bolat'tan 'Made in EU' hamlesi - Avrupa Birliği'nin 'Made in EU' düzenlemesinde Türkiye'nin kapsam dışında kalma ihtimali otomotiv sektörünü harekete geçirdi. Ticaret Bakanı Ömer Bolat, sektör temsilcileriyle birlikte kritik görüşmeler için Almanya'ya gidiyor. Avrupa Birliği'nin (AB) sanayisini korumaya yönelik yeni düzenleme hazırlıkları, Türkiye'nin en önemli ihracat sektörlerinden otomotivde endişe yarattı. Bazı Avrupa ülkelerinin Türkiye'de üretilen ürünleri "Made in EU" kapsamı dışında tutmaya yönelik girişimleri üzerine Ankara ve otomotiv sektörü diplomasi trafiğini hızlandırdı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Ticaret Bakanı Ömer Bolat'ın öncülüğünde, Uludağ Otomotiv Endüstrisi İhracatçıları Birliği (OİB) ve önde gelen otomotiv üreticilerinin temsilcilerinden oluşan heyet, perşembe günü Almanya'ya gidecek. Düzenlemenin Türkiye'yi dışarıda bırakacak şekilde yasalaşması halinde, Türkiye'de üretilen otomobiller ve sanayi parçaları Avrupa'daki bazı kamu destekleri ve teşviklerden yararlanamayabilir. Gümrük Birliği sorunu yeniden gündemde Yeni düzenlemeye ilişkin belirsizlikler, Türkiye ile AB arasındaki Gümrük Birliği'nin güncellenmesi ihtiyacını da yeniden gündeme taşıdı. Ekim ayında 650 milyon dolarlık ihracatla Almanya sektörün en büyük pazarı olurken, Fransa 475 milyon dolar ve Birleşik Krallık 396 milyon dolarla onu takip etti. items.title: Government must act now or lose Royal Mail, former minister warns
items.summary: The former business secretary says "undercutting" by rivals will make Royal Mail "unviable".

items.titleTr: Government must act now or lose Royal Mail, former minister warns
items.summaryTr: The former business secretary says "undercutting" by rivals will make Royal Mail "unviable".
items.articleText: Government must act now or lose Royal Mail, former minister warns - Published Former Business Secretary Peter Kyle has said the government must act urgently to "level the playing field" for Royal Mail or risk the business becoming unviable. He said he was concerned that the firm was being "undercut" by rival parcel delivery firms who did not employ staff under the same conditions. Royal Mail, which is owned by International Distribution Services, has struggled in recent years with increased competition, fewer letters being sent and fines from the regulator for missing delivery targets. A government spokesperson said it would consider whether further reforms are required to the parcel market after the watchdog, Ofcom, publishes its annual monitoring report in December. Kyle had started to prepare officials at the Department for Business and Trade (DBT) to look at the delivery market for parcels shortly before he was replaced in his job by Jonathan Reynolds as business secretary in July. He said a "crunch point" had been reached where the government had to make a decision about whether it wants Royal Mail "to be a viable proposition in the future". He said his review would have looked at where the costs in that market lay and where the profit was being made, to see successful companies upheld "the values of business in Britain today". "If we leave it another few years then Royal Mail will just become unviable and it will just collapse under the weight of having full-time employees," he said. According to Royal Mail, 98% of its 130,000 workers are permanent employees, with rights to benefits including pensions, sick pay and holiday pay. Some other parcel delivery companies use self-employed delivery drivers, with some offering an opt-in service that gives couriers limited additional benefits. Royal Mail is also legally obliged to offer customers a "one price goes anywhere" service across the UK and to deliver first class letters six days a week to every address. Kyle's proposed review would not have considered further changes to Royal Mail's universal service obligations or to terms and conditions for its staff. Royal Mail's performance has improved in recent months but it is still missing its targets for delivering first and second class post. The firm was fined £21m in October 2025 for missing delivery targets in 2024/25. Ofcom agreed last year to scrap second class deliveries on Saturdays and to reduce the target for delivering first class post within a day of collection to 90%. A government spokesperson said the current business secretary had met Royal Mail and the Communication Workers Union, which represents postal workers, last week "to seek timely progress on improving their quality of service and to reiterate our commitment to the company's success." DBT has also launched a consultation on tackling, external what it calls "bogus" self-employment, which it describes as "a practice whereby some businesses mislabel staff as self-employed to avoid statutory obligations". Royal Mail has welcomed the consultation, and a spokesperson for the company claimed some parts of the delivery industry were "driving a race to the bottom" on employment standards and said it would "continue to push for a level playing field, with strong and enforceable standards across the industry." - Royal Mail misses delivery targets again but hails 'encouraging' signs - Published21 August - Hundreds of Royal Mail staff quitting each week under new efficiency plans - Published14 October Many MPs across the UK have reported receiving high volumes of complaints from constituents about missed and delayed deliveries. Shadow business minister Bradley Thomas said that Royal Mail's management needed to address the business's failings. "Customers are being asked time and time again to pay increased prices, yet the service they're receiving is not improving," he said. "Be in no doubt, this is not the fault of the hardworking postmen and women, it's the fault of Royal Mail's management. "Nationalisation isn't the solution to this problem. Instead, we need ministers and Ofcom to bear down on Royal Mail's management to ensure they deliver on the improvements they've promised their customers." The Communication Workers Union, which represents Royal Mail workers, is also putting pressure on ministers, with General Secretary Dave Ward calling for a "new model of ownership".
